draft.title: Leisure
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum had public places where people met for rest and entertainment. These were centres of social life.
Public baths, such as the Stabian Baths at Pompeii, let people wash, exercise and talk. Many townspeople could use them, not only the rich.
Theatres staged plays and other shows. Pompeii had a large theatre and a smaller covered one.
The amphitheatre at Pompeii held gladiator shows and is the oldest surviving stone amphitheatre. Crowds from the town and nearby areas could gather there.
draft.remember: Baths, theatres and the amphitheatre brought people together in shared public life.

a.q: Why are the baths, theatres and amphitheatre described as centres of social life?
opts: People of the town met and mixed there
Only the elite families were allowed to enter
They were used mainly for trade in wine and garum
They were built to honour the gods of the town
a.why: These were public places where people gathered to relax, watch shows and talk. They were not limited to the elite, and their main purpose was leisure, not trade or worship.
a.clue: Think about what happened when people gathered there.

b.q: An archaeologist finds that Pompeii's amphitheatre is the oldest surviving stone amphitheatre. What does this tell us about it?
opts: No older stone amphitheatre survives today
It was the first amphitheatre ever built anywhere
It was built only for use by the elite
It was the only place of entertainment in Pompeii
b.why: Oldest surviving means no older stone one remains today. It does not prove it was the first ever built, since earlier ones may have been lost or made of other materials.
b.clue: Surviving is not the same as first.

a.best: People of the town met and mixed there

b.best: No older stone amphitheatre survives today
